versions.body:
# Theme Runtime Switchover Handoff

This switchover is especially easy to misdescribe as "moving theme runtime to a new path". What is actually being handed off is not a file or a page change, but the basis for making judgments as the known consumers of admin-observability move from the old entry points to candidate paths. Each consumer sees a different entry point; some are historical call names, while others are runtime integration points. Before the handoff, they all count as part of the old path.

The initial inventory started with `config/initializers/devise.rb` and the call names in use at the time. In early records, this file was treated as the starting point for tracing back: someone traced the old entry point from here and recorded it as the owner of the switchover. That judgment was not retained later. The initialization location can explain why that trail was found at the time, but it cannot, on its own, prove that it is responsible for theme runtime, nor can it replace the consumer inventory.

The old records also contain a practice that was not rigorous enough: as soon as one consumer could accept a candidate path, the old entry point was marked as removable. This passage is retained to avoid repeating the same approach to closing out the work. One consumer successfully using a candidate path only shows that migration is possible for that consumer; it does not establish compatibility for the other known consumers, nor does it indicate when the old entry point can be withdrawn.

Read the handoff diagram according to the relationships below. It is a working view of the migration, not an implementation structure diagram.

```text
Before the switchover
admin-observability known consumers
        |
        +--> Old entry point --> Existing theme runtime

During the handoff
Inventoried consumers --> Candidate path --> theme runtime
        |                 |
        |                 +--> Responsible module
        +--> Can still return to the old entry point

Entry points not yet inventoried
        |
        +--> Not deleted as part of this switchover
```

Here, "known consumers" refers only to the consumers of admin-observability already counted in this handoff; it does not assume that undiscovered calls do not exist. Nor is the old entry point equivalent to a source directory; it is the entry method these consumers actually depended on before the switchover. The reason for putting it this way is simple: what needs to be restored during migration is a usable entry point, not some starting point for a search.

## Take inventory first, rather than changing paths first

When taking inventory, record at least four things for each consumer: which old entry point it currently uses; which candidate path it is preparing to try; which module handles that candidate path; and, if rollback is needed, which signal establishes that the consumer has returned to the old path. The first three are easy to write down; the fourth is the one most often missing.

A rollback signal is not "the page seems fine", nor is it the removal of changes to the candidate path. It should let the people handling the handoff distinguish two things: whether the consumer has stopped using the candidate path, and whether the old entry point has once again become the entry method used by that consumer Fang Ke. If these two judgments are conflated, rollback will only establish that the changes were canceled, not whether the caller has been restored.

The inventory table does not need to include every implementation detail, but it should allow the person taking over to answer the following local questions:

| Handoff item | What to record |
| --- | --- |
| Consumer | Confirmed usage location or entry-point description in admin-observability |
| Old entry point | The call name or integration point the consumer currently depends on |
| Candidate path | The alternative entry method planned for this round |
| Responsible module | The module that can modify or restore the candidate path |
| Rollback signal | The basis for determining that the consumer has returned to the old entry point |

A row without a rollback signal must not be considered complete just because the candidate path looks reasonable. A row without a responsible module also cannot be handed to the next person handling it; that would leave "who can restore it" as nothing more than an informal impression.

## Scope of the trial

The candidate path is first tried by a consumer that can roll back independently. Here, "roll back independently" does not mean that it must complete all changes on its own, but that its rollback does not depend on other, not-yet-migrated consumers changing their entry points first. This limits the first trial to a local relationship: whether the candidate path can be integrated, whether the responsible module is clear, and whether the old entry point can still be restored.

There is no need to declare the old path deprecated before the trial. First confirm that this consumer's old entry point is still in the inventory, and write the rollback signal beside the candidate path. After the trial, the observed local result should not be expanded into an overall conclusion either. At most, it shows that the consumer Fang Ke can move from the old entry point to the candidate path and then return according to the recorded signal; the other consumers still need to complete their own handoff items.

The previous sequence of "make changes first, then find out whether rollback is possible" is no longer used. Its problem is not that the candidate path will necessarily fail, but that there is no clearly identified target for restoration when it does fail: someone remembers where changes were made, but has not clearly recorded which call entry point should become usable again. As a result, restoration can easily turn into rolling back implementation details rather than restoring the path the consumer depends on.

## Handling caller compatibility

Known consumers should not all be switched over together. Each item may be in a different state: retaining the old entry point, preparing for a trial, using the candidate path, rolled back, or still in migration because the responsible module and rollback signal are missing. Differences in state are not themselves a problem; erasing those differences is what causes old entry points to be deleted prematurely.

Consumers still retaining the old entry point are not required to add an explanation for the candidate path. They only need to remain visible in the inventory table until their own candidate path, responsible module, and rollback signal are all in place. For consumers that have already completed a trial, do not assume that the old entry point can be removed immediately just because they can roll back. Whether the old entry point can be deleted depends on whether any consumers within the inventory scope still depend on it, not on the result of the first consumer's trial.

The relationship here with DOC-01 is limited to tracing call relationships: when consumer names or old call names are difficult to identify, the records in DOC-01 can be followed to fill in the entry-point descriptions this page needs. This page does not expand that material again into an explanation of call relationships; the handoff table retains only the old entry points, candidate paths, and restoration criteria needed for the switchover.

## How to restore the old path

During rollback, restore the consumer's entry point first, then check the candidate path. This order must not be reversed. If the candidate path is handled first and the consumer's old entry point has not been clearly recorded, the people handling the handoff may reach a state where "the candidate path has stopped", yet be unable to determine whether the consumer has returned to its previously working path.

Perform restoration in the following order:

1. Find the consumer's old entry point and rollback signal in the inventory table.
2. Have the consumer stop depending on the candidate path and return to the recorded old entry point.
3. Use the signal recorded in advance to confirm that the old entry point is usable again.
4. Retain the candidate-path record associated with this rollback; do not rewrite it as though no trial ever took place.
5. If other known consumers still depend on the old entry point, continue to retain it; do not treat this rollback as grounds for deletion.

The fourth step looks like a documentation requirement, but its actual purpose is to prevent the next round from starting with the same candidate path under the mistaken impression that there is no history. Failure or rollback does not automatically invalidate a candidate path; it only indicates that this handoff did not meet the conditions for proceeding. The record should clearly state what was lacking: an incomplete consumer count, an unclear responsible module, or a rollback signal that did not establish a state that could be assessed.

## Handoff criteria

The handoff statement adopted for this round is as follows, serving as a shared constraint on the inventory table and trial records:

> Every handoff names the observable contract, the responsible module, and the rollback signal before implementation work moves.

On this page, observable contract is not an abstract runtime promise, but a relationship that can still be assessed after a specific consumer enters through the old entry point and switches to the candidate path. responsible module does not refer generically to a maintenance team; it identifies the module so that the person taking over knows where to request changes or restoration. rollback signal is not merely a statement that "rollback is possible", but a basis for determining that the consumer is using the old entry point again.

Therefore, all three of the following cases remain in migration: only the candidate path has been found; only who handles the candidate path is known; or how to undo the changes is known, but whether the consumer has returned to the old entry point cannot be clearly stated. The first two cause implementation work to move prematurely, while the last makes it impossible to verify the target of restoration.

By contrast, a consumer can only be marked as having completed this round of the switchover when all four pieces of information are complete, it can perform a trial independently, and restoration of the old entry point after rollback can be confirmed using the signal recorded beforehand. This mark applies only to that consumer and does not automatically cover the other entry points of admin-observability.

## Remaining open issues

The initialization file remains in the early trace-back notes because it explains the original direction of the search; do not elevate it again to the permanent location responsible for theme runtime. This page has also not defined the full boundary of the old entry points as an implementation inventory: it only requires that, when a specific consumer is actually handed over, the entry point that consumer depends on be recorded.

If new consumers of admin-observability are discovered later, add them to the inventory first, then decide whether they need a candidate path. Do not merge a new entry point directly into a completed trial record just to preserve an appearance of uniformity. It needs its own responsible module and rollback signal; if either is missing, continue to treat it as in migration.
